dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Mmm... Detecting the arrival of my two most esteemed friends. Activating chat mode...

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Yes. A director we know invited us to come here and "unwind." Just as well. It's an opportunity to recharge.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Us"...? Wait, but Paimon hasn't seen Lyney anywhere!

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Well... That's his own fault.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: We've been working with this director a lot lately, so my brother took it upon himself to familiarize himself with their style... And ended up watching all of their films.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: All of them? That's some serious dedication right there...

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: The issue is, this director is famous for psychological horror films.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Lyney got so into the plot twists that he didn't sleep properly for three days straight and ended up completely messing up his sleep cycle.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon had no idea Lyney was so into horror films!

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: He tends to get very absorbed in his magic shows, so he probably finds it easy to relate to the characters.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: The way the director uses psychological suggestion is quite similar to how we use it in our shows, after all.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: My brother's still over at the actors' residence. If I had to guess, he's either catching up on sleep or analyzing those films...

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: So that's why I'm out here recharging by myself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well that's a side of Lyney we've never seen before...

choices.text: Now I'm curious about these plot twists myself...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't even think about roping Paimon into this!

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Me neither. I don't like jump scares or stories that give you the chills afterward.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Shouldn't films be relaxing? Something with beautiful visuals, or at least a simple plot that doesn't require too much thinking?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Sounds like Eclectic Escapades would be more to your liking, then. Wanna give it a try?

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Thank you, I've actually done so already. I really liked it.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: But maybe watching others would be even more entertaining...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, is that really that entertaining...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, if you're interested in the attraction, why not become a consultant? That way, you'd get to see more of the visitors' reactions, too!

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: That... doesn't sound like a bad idea. And as it happens, I do have a few days off before filming starts.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: But first, I need to help Lyney pull himself together...

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: I noticed an attraction nearby called "Mellow Manor" that looks really relaxing. Sounds like just what my brother needs to take his mind off those horror films...

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Plus, some magic tricks require animal assistants, so it'll be a chance for me to learn more about their habits.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great idea! If we can get Lyney on board, the Chevalmarin Film Fantasyland will be even more popular than it already is!

choices.text: Why don't we go invite Lyney in person later on?
That priceless look on people's faces as they plummet...
Which scenes is Lyney focusing on in particular?
Were you invited as a special guest too?
